The test image shows large, rounded, silvery-white/pale blue-white galls on the ear of a corn plant, surrounded by dried brown silks. The plant stalk appears otherwise healthy and green.

Key observations:
- Large, swollen, glistening white-silvery galls emerging from the ear position
- Surrounded by dried/matted silk (brown fibrous material)
- Multiple individual galls visible with smooth, silvery-white surface
- No mold, no leaf lesions — isolated ear galls

This perfectly matches **Common_smut**: galls initially covered with glistening, greenish-white or silvery-white tissue, developing on the ear (whole ear or ear tip), caused by local infection. The reference images confirm this — white galls on ears are the hallmark presentation.
